name: generate_mesh
description: Generates a textured mesh from a prompt using AI.

async.description: Run this tool asynchronously and return immediately with a jobId, without blocking on completion. Use this when you want to kick off the work (e.g. several generations at once, or when the user does not need to wait for the result) and continue with other tasks. The tool runs in the background and updates its own UI. Poll the returned jobId with the wait_job_finished tool only when you actually need the final result. If you DO need the result before proceeding, omit this argument (or set it false) and call the tool normally.

maxTriangles.description: The maximum number of triangles for the generated mesh. If provided, this must be between 12 and 20000 (inclusive).

partNames.description: List of part names defining the schema for the generated mesh. Accepts a comma-separated string (e.g. 'body, left wheel, right wheel') or a JSON array of strings (e.g. ['body', 'left wheel', 'right wheel']). Required when segmentation='explicit'. Maximum 8 parts (excess will be truncated).

segmentation.description:
Controls how the mesh is broken into parts. Pick based on the user's wording:
- Omit (or "auto"): user did NOT mention parts/segmentation (e.g. "generate a car"). The tool will derive parts automatically via an internal LLM call.
- "none": user explicitly asked for no parts / a single piece (e.g. "generate a car with no parts", "as one mesh", "single piece").
- "explicit": user named specific parts (e.g. "a car with body and wheels"). You MUST also pass partNames with the user's listed parts (max 8).

size.description: The generation's bounding box size. The generation will try to fit within this volume. Try to approximate a good size based on textPrompt.

studio_id.description: Selects Roblox Studio instance, use the list_roblox_studios tool to get available instances

textPrompt.description: The text prompt describing the mesh to generate.
